_note: INVENTED EXAMPLE. Sam is a made-up bookkeeper and the bakery is made up. Every number is invented to show the format, including the screenshot in images/example-shot.png.

slides.title: Profit is not cash in the bank.
slides.kicker: A profitable year nearly closed a small bakery.

slides.title: Stock paid for months ahead
slides.does: Flour and packaging were bought three months ahead for a bulk discount. The cash left long before the sales came in.
slides.got: The accounts showed a profit. The bank account showed eleven days of runway.

slides.title: A weekly cash sheet
slides.does: One sheet, every Friday: what came in, what went out, what falls due in the next four weeks.

slides.title: Smaller orders, more often
slides.does: Stock is now bought fortnightly. The discount is smaller, and the cash stays put until it is needed.
slides.got: Runway went from eleven days to seven weeks in one quarter.

slides.title: Which one would you pick: the discount or the runway?

caption: INVENTED EXAMPLE CAPTION. The bakery made a profit last year and still nearly closed.
